Each job holds references to chunks, which can be memory-intensive if chunks are large.

Limited by CPU core count and memory bandwidth.
-   **Strengths**: Prevents main thread blocking; prioritizes remeshing to keep visible geometry updated; simple LIFO priority ensures generation jobs are processed first when mixed.

-   **Limitations**: LIFO priority means generation jobs are processed before remesh jobs if pushed in that order (which is the intended behavior for freshness, but might starve remeshes if generation is heavy); no built-in phase yielding (unlike the VoxelTerrainJob Pipeline).
-   **When to use**: When real-time terrain modification requires non-blocking updates and remeshing is frequent.
-   **When not to use**: When frame-time consistency is more important than throughput and jobs can be broken into smaller phases.
It is used in voxel-based game engines to manage the computational cost of terrain generation and meshing.

It solves the problem of blocking the main thread during chunk processing by decoupling job submission from execution [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly describes a multi-threaded job processing system where worker threads pull jobs from a queue and execute them. This architecture inherently decouples the submission of jobs (pushing to the queue) from their execution (worker threads processing the queue). By offloading terrain generation and meshing tasks to these worker threads, the main thread is not blocked during the processing of these chunks, as the heavy lifting is performed asynchronously by the worker threads.
